title: Telegram bot as the first non-fully-authed client
description:
We want to allow users using Telegram (the chat app) to be able to interface with our backend. For this purpose we need to adapt our authentication service to allow non-fully-authed users that authenticate via a special access code (they will provide) + id (their Telegram app will provide so that it uniquely identifies a user) + secret (the Telegram app will know it).
For all sorts and purposes these users can for now access all capabilities that normal users do - they simply don't have an e-mail associated with their account, but at some point we can ask a user to merge accounts - i.e. to provide auth for both Telegram and standard email + password auth to be able to link the two accounts together. In the future we will want to support further logins like these - for instance via Whatsapp or Facebook - but for now these do not need to be implemented, we just need to know that that will come.

features.title: Refactor User Model to Support Multiple Authentication Identities
features.description: To accommodate different authentication methods (Cognito, Telegram, etc.), the user profile model needs to be the central record for a user. Create a new `Identity` entity/interface that links a specific provider (e.g., 'COGNITO', 'TELEGRAM') and a unique identifier (e.g., Cognito `sub`, Telegram ID) to a central `UserProfile`. This involves updating the `UserProfile` interface in `src/profiles/interfaces/user-profile.interface.ts` and modifying the `DynamoDBUserProfilesRepository` to support querying and linking these identities. This is a foundational change to allow a single user to have multiple ways to log in.

features.title: Generalize the Authentication Provider Interface
features.description: Refactor the existing `AuthProvider` interface in `src/auth/interfaces/auth-provider.interface.ts` to be more generic. It should support different authentication strategies beyond the current email/password flow. This may involve creating a new `IAuthStrategy` interface that different providers (like a new `CognitoStrategy` and a future `TelegramStrategy`) will implement. The main `AuthService` will then delegate to the appropriate strategy.

features.title: Implement Telegram Authentication Provider/Strategy
features.description: Create a new `TelegramAuthProvider` or `TelegramAuthStrategy` that implements the newly generalized authentication interface. This provider will contain the logic to authenticate a user via their Telegram ID, a provided access code, and a shared secret stored in environment variables. On successful authentication, it should find an existing user profile linked to that Telegram ID or create a new one if it's the user's first time logging in.

features.title: Add API Endpoint and DTO for Telegram Login
features.description: Create a new endpoint `POST /auth/telegram/login` in `src/auth/auth.controller.ts`. Define a new `TelegramLoginDto` in `src/auth/dto/` to validate the incoming request body, which should include the `telegramId` and `accessCode`. The shared secret should be validated on the backend from configuration and not be part of the DTO.

features.title: Update Auth Service for Telegram Login and JWT Generation
features.description: Modify `src/auth/auth.service.ts` to include a new `loginWithTelegram` method. This method will use the `TelegramAuthProvider` to validate the user's credentials. Upon successful validation, the service must generate a standard JWT containing the central `userId` from the user's profile. This ensures that the session token is uniform, regardless of the login method used, allowing other services and guards to function correctly.

features.title: Legacy code needs to be removed
features.description:
Now that there's the Telegram login - all previous legacy code must be removed leaving only the new ways of login - i.e. via Telegram and via Cognito. No deprecated or legacy code should be left.

Scan the whole repository and clean things up so that they are cohesive, modularised and easy to read and understand.

features.title: There needs to be a `/health` endpoint
features.description: For AWS to be able to see that the backend is healthy we need a  `/health` endpoint that simply returns 200 OK . The `/` endpoint should do the same.
